properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 25 at 12:36AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.
Relative humidity values are forecast to drop into the 30 to 40
percent range, especially near and north of the Interstate 10 and
12 corridors. The 20 ft wind forecast is expected to remain at or
below 10 mph in most areas, which should limit critical fire
weather conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that
may ignite.

Numerous local burn bans are in place and continue to expand
across LA and MS due to ongoing drought conditions. This now
includes East Feliciana, Iberville, Pointe Coupee, St. Helena, St
Tammany, Tangipahoa, Washington and West Feliciana Parishes along
with Wilkinson, Amite, Pike, and Walthall Counties. Regardless,
outdoor burning is strongly not recommended this afternoon, and
all local restrictions followed.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS TODAY

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 25 at 3:01PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Tropical Storm In-fa (30W) is beginning to exit the northern Marshall
Islands as it moves northwest, currently passing near Bikini Atoll.
However, hazardous conditions continue across the region, with
scatterometry this morning showing fresh to strong southwest to west
winds across the northernmost islands and atolls of the RMI. Seas
will remain hazardous to small craft across the area through tonight
as In-fa moves away, due to elevated wind waves and west to
southwest swell, and inter-island travel is strongly discouraged.
Locally heavy showers may produce sudden, strong to near-gale
gusts, leading to locally dangerous conditions. These conditions will
diminish over the next few days as In-fa moves farther away.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header
WTPQ31 PGUM.

properties.areaDesc: Eddy, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 24 at 10:23PM MDT until October 25 at 1:30AM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Eddy County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 130 AM MDT.

* At 1023 PM MDT, A trained weather spotter reported several inches
of standing water from the Charley White Draw over Highway 82 west
of Hope. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northwestern Eddy County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

flooding is occurring along Council Road east of Nome, causing

peaked and will gradually drop into Sunday. While water levels

residences should not be impacted as the water remains below
the berm. Even though water levels drop somewhat, they will
remain normal through early next week. Localized beach erosion
may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...South to southwest winds will continue to
gust up to 40 mph through the weekend. Strong winds continue
into early next week.

expected along the San Juan River between Four Corners and Mexican
Hat. This is an emergency situation!

* WHERE...Western Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...

attempt to cross.

Juan River from Four Corners to Mexican Hat. The San Juan River

reaching Montezuma Creek around 5 am MDT Sunday, cresting between
Bluff and Mexican Hat Sunday afternoon and peaking at Mexican Hat

record levels. The San Juan River will rise above flood stage
Sunday morning and continue to rise Sunday afternoon to moderate
flood stage, peaking above major flood stage at Mexican Hat by 5
pm Sunday evening.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
San Juan River

Aneth.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 9:21PM AST until October 27 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches along the northwest to northeast coast of
Puerto Rico and Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH TUESDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Hawaii in Hawaii, HI; Oahu in Honolulu, HI; Kauai, HI; Maui, HI
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 24 at 3:10PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
ESFHFO

A significant pattern change is expected Monday night through at
least Thursday as deep tropical moisture is brought north. A
combination of surface lows and troughs will bring exceptionally
moist air over the eastern end of the state beginning Monday night
and extending to all islands Tuesday. Heavy rain and thunderstorms
are possible throughout this period. Models have not converged on
details yet, so exact locations, timing, and rainfall amounts are not
certain. Please be prepared for periods of heavy rain this coming
week.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through the
Internet (weather.gov/hawaii), local media, social media, or NOAA

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 8:58PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Saturday was 3.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.6 feet
Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1000 AM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Outer Banks
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 24 at 8:43PM EDT until October 25 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to
8 feet in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2
feet of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves expected in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT Wednesday. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT Sunday through Sunday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer
head first into the bottom causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will continue to rise with a
King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-week. The
morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily tides.
King Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 24 at 8:43PM EDT until October 25 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to
8 feet in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2
feet of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves expected in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT Wednesday. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT Sunday through Sunday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Ocean overwash impacts will continue through at least
Tuesday, especially around high tide, in areas where dunes have
been compromised. NC-12 between the Basnight Bridge and Rodanthe
remains closed. The next high tide is around 700 AM Sunday. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or
surfer head first into the bottom causing neck and back
injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will continue to rise with a
King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-week. The
morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily tides.
King Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 8:43PM EDT until October 28 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 to 3 feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Onslow County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT
Wednesday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT
Sunday through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and
low lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and
homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow
flooding. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will continue to rise with a King
Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-week. The morning
high tide will be the highest of the two daily tides. King
Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

properties.description:

waves 1 to 2 feet expected on Lake Moultrie.

* WHERE...Lake Moultrie.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds and rough waves on Lake Moultrie will create
hazardous conditions for small craft.

and rough waves can overturn small craft.

properties.description:

* WHERE...In Florida, Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler, Coastal Nassau,

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Horry
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 24 at 7:28PM EDT until October 25 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, Strong
north to south longshore current. There is also a Moderate Risk
of rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Horry County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM EDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 6 AM EDT Sunday through
Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Vulnerable causeways to and from local beaches will
experience minor coastal flooding. Low-lying roads and
locations along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal
creeks will observe minor coastal flooding. Some roads may
become impassable. Check with local officials for the latest
information regarding coastal flood impacts and closures.
Longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties, and other hazardous areas. It may
sweep swimmers off their feet, making it difficult to return
to shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Caution should be used when in or near the water. Check with
lifeguards before entering the ocean for possible hazards you may
be swept into.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 2:46PM MST until October 26 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues. This
rainfall occurred on Wednesday and Thursday.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST Sunday Night /100 AM MDT Monday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.
Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 240 PM MST /340 PM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to fall this evening. However, downstream
impacts will continue at Navajo Route 71 to Birdsprings through
at least Sunday.
- Flooding is occurring along the Little Colorado River.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 2:00pm MST /3:00pm MDT/ the stage was 18.34 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: The river is cresting now and is forecast to fall
through this evening.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

waterways.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:07 AM
Sunday 10/25, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 11:39 AM
Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43
PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up to 1.0 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 24 at 3:35PM EDT until October 26 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 12 feet
expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint Lucie, Coastal
Martin, Mainland Southern Brevard and Southern Brevard Barrier
Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 8 PM this evening to 8 PM EDT Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 AM Sunday to 8 PM EDT
Monday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 11:16AM AKDT until October 26 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 2.0 to 3.0 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 40 mph southwest winds
with gusts up to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...7 PM Sunday to 7 AM AKDT Monday, highest water levels
expected around midnight Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Relatively, the area to see higher water
levels is expected to be Kipnuk. The most likely scenario is for
water levels to be 2.0 to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide
line. Kwigillingok may see water levels of 1.0 to 2.0 ft above
the normal highest tide line. The peak will be around midnight
Monday morning, coinciding with high tide. Following this
system, steady southwesterly flow is expected to continue for
the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through Tuesday, which may slow
the ability for flood waters to recede.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 24 at 12:23PM EDT until October 26 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 8 feet.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 5 PM EDT this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Monday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, from 5 PM this afternoon to 8 PM EDT
Monday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Flagler; Northeast Coastal St. Johns; Southeast Coastal St. Johns
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 24 at 12:23PM EDT until October 26 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns and
Southeast Coastal St. Johns Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 5 PM EDT this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Monday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, from 5 PM this afternoon to 8 PM EDT
Monday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches; Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 3:28AM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Coastal areas of Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara,
and San Luis Obispo Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be Monday
through Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal
Flood Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf
develops.
properties.instruction:
Listen to advice from local officials. Do NOT drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Mesa, CO; Montrose, CO; Grand, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 4:09PM MDT until October 25 at 10:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Along the Dolores River from Bedrock to the confluence with
the Colorado River in:
Southwestern Mesa County in west central Colorado...
West Central Montrose County in west central Colorado...
East Central Grand County in east central Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Dolores River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 408 PM MDT, Flooding is expected along the Dolores River.
Highway 141 could see impacts along the river as well as the 141
bridge through Gateway. Water levels are forecast to continue to
rise through Gateway this evening and peak overnight. The river
is running fast and high.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Dolores River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gateway and Highway 141
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM MDT SUNDAY

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 23 at 11:03AM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday during high tides.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur in the
morning hours.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal residents in the warned area should
be alert for rising water and take appropriate action to protect
life and property. High tides each day will occur in the
morning. Tides may be anywhere from 1 to 1.7 feet above
predicted.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 11:31AM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

San Juan River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Farmington.

* WHEN...From this morning to Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.5 feet, Overbank flow is occurring from just below
the confluence of the Animas and San Juan Rivers at Farmington, and
continuing downriver through Shiprock. At this water level, the
fast flow can result in river bank erosion but otherwise minor
flood damage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 5.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.2 feet
late tomorrow evening.
- Action stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM THIS MORNING TO SUNDAY AFTERNOON
